PullRequest.Title: Add regression tests for single-item Activity Bar overflow
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #187737

The current composite bar already avoids an "Additional Views" overflow with a single item: each action is the same size as the overflow control, so once views overflow one slot goes to the overflow control and at least two views are always hidden. This PR adds regression tests (`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/compositeBar.test.ts`, suite "CompositeBar overflow") that lock that in across classic, compact, modern, modern compact, modern sidebar-right and modern compact-density layouts. They sweep heights to check that exactly one hidden view never happens, that the overflow menu shows every hidden view, and that a selected overflow view is promoted back into the bar. There are no production changes.

Runtime screenshots across all six layouts confirmed the same behavior: at fit−1, two views are hidden (Run and Debug, Extensions), no height leaves exactly one view hidden, and selecting Extensions promotes it back into the bar.

### How to test

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/compositeBar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/activitybarPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/compositeBarActions.test.ts`: passed (40 passing, 1 pending)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/compositeBar.test.ts`: passed (no problems)

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser unit-test execution of the new CompositeBar overflow suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test module is loaded by the browser runner and its Mocha tests run before the file can complete. The height sweep is on that test's critical path: 1,764 sequential calls to CompositeBar.layout followed by DOM-label inspection, with overflow-menu action materialization while overflow is present.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test data: four strides (48, 28, 44, 40), ten composites, and 11 * stride + 1 heights per stride, totaling 1,764 iterations. Each iteration scans at most ten rendered labels and handles at most ten overflow items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha executes the loop sequentially because each iteration is awaited. The runner can distribute different test files across browser workers, but this file is claimed by one worker and has no internal parallelism or burst of external work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold browser-test page the module is imported once and product stylesheets are preloaded by the runner. Within the page, module/style imports are cached. Each bar is freshly constructed per test/stride; menu actions are regenerated per overflow inspection, but cardinality is fixed and all objects are disposed or become collectible at test/suite teardown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the fixed repeated DOM/CPU work from the added loop and traced CompositeBar/layout/menu call path; high confidence that no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached by the changed test body.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser-test wall time and allocation volume are not measured. The loop is bounded and small per iteration, so any CI latency increase is limited to this test file.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The PR adds bounded test-only CPU, DOM queries, and action allocations; it does not create a realistic shipped-product performance regression or an unbounded/large test workload.

Scenarios.Scenario: End-user Activity Bar layout, overflow menu opening, and selecting a hidden view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: In the shipped application, Activity Bar resize/layout and overflow-menu interaction continue through the existing CompositeBar implementation. The new file is test code and is not imported by production, so no added work is on the user interaction or rendering critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Realistic activity-view count and resize/input frequency are unchanged by the PR; effective production cardinality is identical before and after the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No production scheduling, limiter, queue, listener, or concurrency behavior changes. Existing layout remains synchronous as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No production cache key, cache state, invalidation, coalescing, or lifecycle changes. The test harness's per-test objects do not survive into product execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete changed-file inventory contains only one newly added browser test file and no production changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality; runtime product cost is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The regression tests exercise existing rendering behavior but introduce no production CPU, memory, rendering, layout, I/O, network, or startup cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the full one-file diff. Examined the pixel-height sweep, DOM/layout operations, overflow-menu allocation path, suite disposal, browser-runner module/style loading, and test-file concurrency. No actionable performance regression was introduced.
